turnaround_reason: Lululemon fell ~48% from ~$226 to ~$118 as US/Americas demand stalled (Q1 2026 Americas comps -5%) and the company cut full-year guidance, even as international (China +30%, intl comps +13%) stays strong. It's now cheap for the franchise at ~9.5x trailing / ~10.5x forward earnings with heavy insider buying.
bullish_points: Premium global brand at a trough valuation (P/E ~9.5, well below its historical range) with international still compounding fast (China revenue +30%)
Strong insider buying: 65,369 shares purchased across 27 transactions vs 622 sold in last 6 months
Healthy balance sheet ($1.51B cash vs $2.14B debt) and deep options liquidity (call OI 8,652) for structured entries
Q2 FY2026 earnings due early September — a hard near-term catalyst that could mark the US bottom if comps stabilize
bearish_points: US turnaround is unconfirmed: North America guided to high-single-digit full-year decline, low-double-digit decline in Q2
EPS fell 35% YoY in Q1 on margin pressure; product launches criticized for failing to excite shoppers
Sits ~24% below its 200d MA and below its 100d MA — no trend confirmation, still basing
Tariff/margin headwinds and a still-soft US consumer could extend the comp decline
catalyst: Q2 FY2026 earnings and holiday product/newness cycle; a stabilization or beat on US comps would reprice the stock off trough multiples
suggested_trade: Small starter spot into earnings; keep dry powder to size up if Q2 shows US comps flattening. Aggressive players can use defined-risk calls given liquid chain.
key_risk: US comps keep deteriorating and guidance is cut again, confirming brand fatigue rather than a cyclical dip
would_skip_if: Q2 US comps come in worse than the guided low-double-digit decline with no forward improvement
